title: Google Research develops AI system for passive hypertension detection
excerpt: The AI-PPG-ACC-HTN system uses smartwatch sensors to identify signs of high blood pressure without requiring cuff calibration.
bodyHtml:
Google Research announced on November 5, 2026, a new artificial intelligence system designed to detect signs of hypertension using consumer smartwatch sensors. The system, titled AI-PPG-ACC-HTN, utilizes photoplethysmography to track blood volume changes and accelerometry to capture mechanical heart vibrations.

In a study published in Nature, researchers validated the system against 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring. The study involved 196 participants across five US sites and demonstrated that the system achieves accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuff-based diagnostic workflows for initial and confirmatory screening.

The system uses a two-stage machine learning approach. Stage 1 involves self-supervised pre-training using a 1-D deep convolutional neural network. Stage 2 involves person-level aggregation and classification. During confirmatory testing, the system achieved a sensitivity of 78.4%, a specificity of 90.9%, and a positive predictive value of 96.7%.
topic: Detecting signs of hypertension using wearable sensors
